note: Literature demonstrates that GTPBP2-deficient patients have been referred for Joubert syndrome testing due to false-positive identification of the molar tooth sign.

evidence.text: D'Abrusco et al. identified non-ciliary neurodevelopmental gene variants, including pathogenic variants in GTPBP2, among patients inappropriately referred for Joubert syndrome testing due to misinterpretation of neuroimaging findings as the molar tooth sign.

source.title: Get your molar tooth right: Joubert syndrome misdiagnosis unmasked by whole-exome sequencing
source.quote: Here, we present six cases referred for JS genetic testing based on inappropriate recognition of MTS. While the analysis of JS-related genes was negative, whole-exome sequencing (WES) disclosed pathogenic variants in other genes causative of distinct brain malformative conditions with partial clinical and neuroradiological overlap with JS.

numbers.metric: cases referred for JS testing based on inappropriate MTS recognition

evidence.text: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome is characterized by motor developmental delay, intellectual disability, hypotonia, and skeletal/visual abnormalities across the 28 reported cases in the literature.

source.title: Jaberi-Elahi syndrome: Exploring a novel GTPBP2 mutation and a literature review
source.quote: A large numbers of patients manifest motor development delay (26/28), sparse hair (26/28), and speech disorder (24/28). Moreover, a significant fraction of patients suffer from intellectual disability (23/28), hypotonia (23/28), skeletal problems (23/28), and visual impairment (18/28).
